A key

stem: A graph has 1000 vertices but each vertex is joined to only 3 others. Which representation uses less memory?

stem: In an undirected graph the adjacency matrix is symmetrical about its main diagonal.

stem: A dictionary may contain the same key twice with two different values.
explanation: False. Keys are unique. Adding an existing key replaces its value.

stem:
The weighted graph of bus stops has these edges (minutes):

| Edge | Weight |
|:-:|:-:|
| P – Q | 6 |
| P – R | 3 |
| Q – S | 2 |
| R – S | 7 |
| S – T | 4 |
| Q – T | 9 |

It is stored as an adjacency matrix. What value is in row R, column S?
workedSolution: The edge R – S has weight 7, and the graph is undirected, so row R, column S holds 7.
hints: Look in the row of the matrix for P and the column for R.

stem: How many entries are there altogether in the adjacency list of a graph with 5 vertices and 6 edges (each undirected edge is listed under both ends)?
explanation: 12 entries.
workedSolution: 6 edges × 2 = 12 entries. (A matrix would need 5 × 5 = 25 cells.)
hints: Each undirected edge appears under both of its vertices.

stem: A hash table has 8 slots (numbered 0 to 7). The hashing function adds the ASCII codes of the characters in the key and takes the remainder when divided by 8. The sum of the codes of the key `Nyasha` is 612. In which slot is it stored?
hints: Add the ASCII codes (given) and divide by the size, taking the remainder.

stem: Name the method of dealing with a collision by using the next free slot.
explanation: Linear probing.

stem: Compare an adjacency matrix with an adjacency list as ways of storing a graph. [4]

points.description: A matrix uses n × n cells whatever the number of edges
A list uses space only for the edges that exist, so it is smaller for a graph with few edges
In a matrix, whether an edge exists is found directly with one access
In a list, the neighbour list has to be searched to find an edge

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A matrix needs n × n cells whatever the number of edges, while a list uses space only for the edges that exist. A matrix shows whether an edge exists with one access, but a list has to be searched.

explanation: Memory and look-up time.
hints: Compare memory and the speed of checking an edge.

stem: Describe how a dictionary can be implemented as a hash table. [3]

points.description: A hashing function is applied to the key to give an index into an array
The key-value pair is stored in that position
If two keys give the same index (a collision), the next free slot is used (linear probing) or the keys are chained in a list

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A hashing function turns the key into an index of an array, and the key and value are stored there. If two keys give the same index, the next free slot is used or the keys are chained together.

explanation: Hash, store, collisions.
hints: Say how the index is found, what a collision is and how it is dealt with.

stem: Explain how a queue can be implemented using a linked list. [4]

points.description: Each item is a node holding data and a pointer to the next node
A head pointer refers to the front node and a tail pointer to the last
Enqueue adds a new node after the tail and moves the tail pointer
Dequeue returns the data in the head node and moves the head pointer to the next node

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each item is a node with a data value and a pointer to the next node. A head pointer marks the front and a tail pointer marks the last node. Enqueue adds a node after the tail and moves the tail pointer, and dequeue returns the head node's data and moves the head pointer to the next node.

explanation: Nodes, pointers, enqueue, dequeue.
hints: Think about what operations are needed and what is stored.

stem:
A hash table with 8 slots (0 to 7) stores names. The hashing function adds the ASCII codes of the characters of the key and takes the remainder when divided by 8. The values are:

| Key | Sum of ASCII codes | Sum MOD 8 |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Sipho | 515 | 3 |
| Kudzi | 519 | 7 |
| Tinashe | 716 | 4 |
| Blessing | 823 | 7 |
| Anesu | 508 | 4 |

The keys are stored in the order Sipho, Kudzi, Tinashe, Blessing, Anesu. If a slot is taken, the next slot is tried (and the search wraps round after slot 7).

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the slots in which Sipho and Kudzi are stored.
parts.explanation: Each key goes to the slot given by its hash value, as neither slot is taken.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: In which slot is Blessing stored? (Remember that the search wraps round after slot 7.)
parts.workedSolution: Blessing's hash value is 7; that slot is taken, so the next free slot is used: 0.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: In which slot is Anesu stored?
parts.workedSolution: Anesu's hash value is 4; the slot used is 5.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain how the program finds Blessing again.

points.description: It applies the hashing function to the key to get the starting slot
It looks at that slot and the following slots (wrapping round) until it finds Blessing (or an empty slot)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It applies the hashing function to Blessing to get the starting slot, then checks that slot and the following ones, wrapping round, until Blessing is found.

explanation: Hashing with linear probing on a table of 8 slots.
hints: Compute the remainder for each key, then place the keys in order.
A taken slot means the next one is tried.
